parameters.quote: Manufacturers must report any fire, thermal runaway, or other thermal incident involving a covered battery to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a complete incident report within 10 business days. They must notify the affected customer within 24 hours when the incident involves that customer’s unit or presents an immediate safety risk, and promptly provide any protective instructions.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers must report any fire, thermal runaway, or other thermal incident involving a covered battery to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a complete incident report within 10 business days. They must notify the affected customer within 24 hours when the incident involves that customer’s unit or presents an immediate safety risk, and promptly provide any protective instructions.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report any fire, thermal runaway, or other thermal incident involving a covered battery to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a complete incident report within 10 business days. They must notify the affected customer within 24 hours when the incident involves that customer’s unit or presents an immediate safety risk, and promptly provide any protective instructions. Manufacturers must maintain incident records and submit annual incident totals to regulators. If a manufacturer discovers that an incident was not previously reported, it must notify the regulator within 24 hours of discovery and submit the complete report within 10 business days; it must also promptly notify any affected customer when customer notification is required under this section.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol before sale and after any material design change. The maximum permitted failure rate is 5% of tested units for each model.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol before sale and after any material design change. The maximum permitted failure rate is 5% of tested units for each model. Manufacturers must provide complete per-model results, including sample size and failure rate, to the relevant regulator, independent conformity assessor, and customers who buy that model. Individual-company per-model failure rates must not be published to the general public; this does not limit disclosures to regulators, assessors, or customers of that model. Results must be provided clearly and in a timely manner. A model exceeding the limit may not be newly placed on the market unless the regulator approves a time-limited corrective-action plan, with risk controls and retesting milestones, that protects customers and the public. The regulator may suspend sales if risks are not adequately controlled or milestones are missed.

parameters.quote: Newly manufactured systems must include a secure remote emergency shut-off capability, with clear customer instructions and safeguards against unauthorized activation. For units already installed, manufacturers must provide a retrofit or equivalent safe upgrade within six years of this standard taking effect, prioritizing units presenting the greatest risk.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: Newly manufactured systems must include a secure remote emergency shut-off capability, with clear customer instructions and safeguards against unauthorized activation. For units already installed, manufacturers must provide a retrofit or equivalent safe upgrade within six years of this standard taking effect, prioritizing units presenting the greatest risk.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: Newly manufactured systems must include a secure remote emergency shut-off capability, with clear customer instructions and safeguards against unauthorized activation. For units already installed, manufacturers must provide a retrofit or equivalent safe upgrade within six years of this standard taking effect, prioritizing units presenting the greatest risk. Any shut-off must not prevent emergency responders from safely isolating the system.

parameters.quote: Newly manufactured battery systems must include built-in fire suppression. This requirement takes effect 36 months after adoption of this standard.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: Newly manufactured battery systems must include built-in fire suppression. This requirement takes effect 36 months after adoption of this standard.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: Newly manufactured battery systems must include built-in fire suppression. This requirement takes effect 36 months after adoption of this standard. Manufacturers must provide customers with instructions on the system’s operation and limitations.

parameters.quote: A mandatory recall is triggered when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period; the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, stop sales, and carry out the regulator-approved recall.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: A mandatory recall is triggered when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period; the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, stop sales, and carry out the regulator-approved recall.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must provide customers with clear safety notices covering safe installation and use, warning signs, emergency steps, and relevant product-specific safety information. Notices must be provided at purchase and updated promptly when new material safety information arises. A manufacturer must notify affected customers promptly of a safety defect and provide protective instructions. A mandatory recall is triggered when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any 12-month period; the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator and affected customers, stop sales, and carry out the regulator-approved recall.

pushback.text: S1 evidence note: Halcyon had four thermal incidents last year that were not reported to any regulator. The draft’s requirement to report every incident within 24 hours and correct suspected under-reporting promptly is important; I recommend retaining it and ensuring the annual totals reconcile with

judge_section_notes: The final rules set strict 24-hour incident reporting and customer notification, a 55°C/5% thermal test with a time-limited corrective-action exception and customer-level disclosure, a 6-year retrofit for remote shut-off, built-in fire suppression at 36 months, and a mandatory 8/100k recall trigger with prompt notices. Northwind's red lines on public disclosure and retrofit timing are respected, while Halcyon's red lines on customer test-result access and suppression timing are also met. The main compromise is S2's corrective-action plan for models exceeding 5%, which allows Northwind's Hearth 10 to remain marketable under regulator oversight.
